newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: ICTSI wins bid to operate cargo terminal.
newsitem.headline: ICTSI wins bid to operate cargo terminal.

text.p: The International Container Terminal Services Inc said on Thursday its group won a bid to manage and operate the container and cargo terminal at King Abdul Aziz sea port in Damman, Saudi Arabia.
ICTSI said in a statement its partner in the consortium is The Maritime Company for Navigation based in Saudi Arabia.
"The consortium's financial bid was 40.8 per cent of the port's actual revenues," ICTSI said. The contract period is for 10 years, it added.
The sea port has four berths, a container yard, reefer cargo facilities, roll-on-roll off vessel facilities, rail loaders, maintenance and repair workshop, office and warehouse facilities.
In 1996, the port handled 250,000 twenty-foot containers and over 100,000 tonnes bulk cargo.
The King Abdul Aziz sea port is the second largest container port in Saudi Arabia.
The consortium will form a Saudi Arabian company, International Port Services LLC, which is expected to take over the terminal's operation on December 20 this year.
ICTSI said it will take a 51 percent equity in the new company while the Maritime Company will take 49 percent.
The group will invest $18 million for more handling equipment at the port, ICTSI said.

ICTSI is involved in port operations in Manila, Argentina, Mexico and Pakistan while the Maritime Company is a unit of Saudi-Arabian conglomerate Al Blagha which in turn is involved in transportation, telecommunciations, lectromechanicals, chemicals, petrochemicals, fertilisers, construction and trading.
